label: Defined contribution plan: employer’s minimum annual contribution
unit: share of the employee’s annual total wages
appliesTo: Employees enrolled in a defined contribution (DC) retirement pension plan
why: A DC balance is not calculated backwards from a final salary, so the thing to audit is whether each year's contribution was actually paid at this level. Under-contribution accumulates silently across years and is the characteristic DC dispute, in the way that a mis-stated average wage is the characteristic dispute on ordinary severance.

history.source: Act on the Guarantee of Workers’ Retirement Benefits, DC contribution requirement
history.note: At least one twelfth of the employee's total annual wages, paid into the employee's DC account. Investment gains and losses on the account then belong to the employee — which is why the contribution record, not the final balance, is what shows whether the employer met its obligation.
